question: When a feature is added to a slice or taken out of it after its plan exists, what must the plan play do with the stories of that slice?
answer: When a feature comes into the slice, the plan play adds one story for it, so that each feature of the slice has a story; it makes no second story for a feature that has one; and nothing goes to the tracker before the product owner's yes. What it does with the story of a feature that goes out is not set by the model: the product owner says.

question: In what form must the eval play write the eval of a slice, so that a person can run it from the outside?
answer: The eval is written in the plan's evals folder (.garura/project/plans/<plan-id>/evals/<slug>/). For each goal and expectation of the stories, and each failure condition of the slice's hidden file, it holds one check run from the outside on the slice's surface (for Garura often a run of the play on a test project), or a note that it cannot be tested yet. The layout of the file itself is not set by the model: the product owner says.

source.text: - Partly ready: it is ready, but the check found gaps that do not stop work, such as no domain or an ICE with no context yet. The ICE goes forward, and work starts. The check lists each gap to fix later. (Our proposal: what counts as a gap is not yet agreed.)

around.text:

- How we will know: a ready check gives one answer for each capability and feature. It reads the links, the needs and the status of each part, and applies the rules above.
  - Ready: it serves a confirmed business intent, and everything it needs is done. The agent intent (ICE) goes forward, and work starts.
  - Partly ready: it is ready, but the check found gaps that do not stop work, such as no domain or an ICE with no context yet. The ICE goes forward, and work starts. The check lists each gap to fix later. (Our proposal: what counts as a gap is not yet agreed.)
  - Not ready: it serves no confirmed business intent, or something it needs is not done. The ICE does not go forward, and work stops until the cause is fixed. The page itself is kept.

## Inputs / Outputs
- In: the epic of the slice, with its feature-to-story map, and its stories. The map joins each hidden-file entry (by its feature) to its story (ontology v11, Q36).
- In: the slice's hidden file (failure-and-recovery.md) from the plan's evals folder.
- Out: one eval for the business intent in `.garura/project/plans/<plan-id>/evals/<slug>/`.
- Out (when needed): a handoff plan, which never names a failure condition, its id or its check.
- Thin: the format of the eval and of the handoff plan is not set yet.

## Rules & behavior

source.text:
- The eval checks from the outside, on the slice's surface. For Garura that surface is often a play, so the eval runs the play on a test project.
- The running eval reaches the slice only through its usage guide (`guides/<slug>.md`).
- When the eval cannot test a goal, an expectation or a failure condition yet, it says so.

around.text:
## Rules & behavior
- The play runs after /shape-plan, on its own.
- It reads only the epic, its stories and the hidden file. It never reads an ICE page, the usage guide or the code.
- The eval checks from the outside, on the slice's surface. For Garura that surface is often a play, so the eval runs the play on a test project.
- The running eval reaches the slice only through its usage guide (`guides/<slug>.md`).
- When the eval cannot test a goal, an expectation or a failure condition yet, it says so.
- Until eval encryption (#828) exists, only a read rule keeps builders out of the evals folder.

## Acceptance criteria

trace.asked: what each check must cover
trace.found: each goal, expectation and failure condition has a check or a note that it cannot be tested yet

source.text: - Given the eval, when a person reads it, then each goal and expectation of the stories, and each failure condition of the hidden file, has a check or a note that it cannot be tested yet.

around.text:
## Acceptance criteria
- Given a plan with an epic and its stories, when the product owner runs /shape-eval, then the eval is in the plan's evals folder.
- Given the eval, when a person reads it, then each goal and expectation of the stories, and each failure condition of the hidden file, has a check or a note that it cannot be tested yet.
- Given the build plays, when a person reads their inputs, then none names the evals folder.
